neighborhood_overview: A four block stroll takes you to Golden Gate Park and its world-class museums  (DeYoung Art Museum and California Academy of Sciences), along with its meadows and flower gardens. A short drive takes you to Ocean Beach (expert-level surfing or tension-relieving walks), to the Golden Gate Bridge and Chrissy Field,to Fisherman's Wharf, or to the restaurants, bars, and shops of Union Square, North Beach, Haight-Ashbury, and Fillmore Street. Challenging and well-kept public golf courses include The Presidio Golf Cours
host_about: We are a family of four. We enjoy traveling, but also the activities our neighborhood, city, and region provide.  These include beach walks, Bay swimming, surfing,snowboarding, attending sports events (GO GIANTS!), and visiting museums. Before the advent of Airbnb, we hosted exchange students from France, Spain, and Paraguay, and hosted guests from North Africa, along with family from other parts of the U.S. and Mexico.  We love cooking (and eating).  We can help  you find the best food from fine-dining, to hip dining, to casual comfy to food trucks.  We love a broad range of music, and we can steer you in the direction of live music offerings.  We see it as our obligation to be present when you need us, and (nearly) invisible when you do not.  One of us is fluent in Spanish, the other is functional in Spanish and French.

host_about:
Hi – I’m Derek.  I’ve been in San Francisco since 2002, so not quite a native, but pretty close by SF standards!

By day, I am a corporate attorney.  In my free time, I am an amateur magician who loves to rescue dogs, travel the world, workout, play the piano, take pictures, eat great food and drink great wine.  I also loving watching movies, binge watching pretty much anything on Netflix, cooking and mixology. 

I have stayed in Airbnbs all over the world and love the flexibility it allows frequent travelers.  Many of my trips would not have been possible if not for Airbnb.   As a host, I love to work with fellow travel lovers to experience all the amazing features of Northern California and extend the same hospitality I received throughout the world. 

I live up the street from this home and my co-host Maryann and I are available for anything you need.  We are very familiar with the City and surrounding area.   We can recommend restaurants, the best time for experiencing local attractions, hikes, museums and more!  And, if you are a wine lover, Maryann has multiple wine certifications and has amazing recommendations for wine tastings both in San Francisco and Napa/Sonoma.  Ask us anything you need! 

My favorite part of the property is the separate structure we call the “Movie Cabin.”  I love curling up with my dogs and watching a blockbuster movie on the projection television.  The Movie Cabin can also be used as a yoga/meditation studio or an office.  There is outdoor seating next to the Movie Cabin where you can enjoy a glass of wine and watch the sun set or enjoy your morning coffee with a great book.  The Movie Cabin is cozy and has a full bath.  You may end up spending all your time in the Movie Cabin!

Please send us any questions you have and we really hope you choose to spend your time in San Francisco with us!  We would love to host you and your family/friends – including your furry family and friends!

Visitors say they appreciate our clean and well appointed home and our knowledge of the city and professional attitude.

We think this is because we still live there part of each year and keep the house comfortable and well maintained not only for our guests but for ourselves as well. We are also proud of our garden, keeping it maintained even while we are away. We paint, scrape, clean, renew, update and replace parts of the house every time we come to visit. We think it shows. 

Our guests certainly enjoy our home. Read the reviews! 170 Five Star ratings on HA/VR and 75 on TA. Finally, if you are bringing a car, you will absolutely love our little garage (for economy to mid-size cars). Parking rules in SF can make you dizzy. If you don't bring a car - great! - hop on the bus one block from the front door and head downtown or to the beach.

You can read more about our home at YourHomeInSanFrancisco. 
Thanks!

neighborhood_overview:
It is east of the more famous Haight-Ashbury, which is also known as the Upper Haight. The name derives from the significant elevation change as Haight Street climbs steeply from Scott Street to Buena Vista Park.

The area straddles a shallow valley between Mint Hill and Upper Haight, sloping down from Oak Street (north) toward Duboce (south). Duboce Park, toward the corner of Duboce and Scott, is a grassy park containing a children's playground, dog park, and the Harvey Milk Recreational Arts Building.

Adjacent neighborhoods include the Western Addition/Alamo Square to the north; Duboce Triangle to the south; Hayes Valley to the east; and the Upper Haight to the west.

neighborhood_overview:
The Potrero Hill district is one of the most unique neighborhoods in San Francisco and has gone through several changes from working class to the newer family oriented direction since the 1990's

Potrero Hill is one of the sunniest neighborhoods in San Francisco. It is insulated from our famous fog and chill from the ocean and gives some of the most spectacular views of downtown and the bay bridge. If you are up for a few hills it can be a great walking experience and the ever growing "hub" of 18th street is always a great place to start a day.

One of the best parts of Potrero Hill is that it is a neighborhood further from the "hustle and bustle" so it has a quiet and sleepy feel but you are never more than a few minutes from the fray.

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to the vibrant Castro neighborhood in San Francisco, one of the most historic and diverse areas in the city. Known for its rich cultural heritage, this neighborhood is a popular destination for locals and tourists alike. The Castro has played a significant role in the LGBTQ+ community since the 1970s, and it continues to be a symbol of acceptance, inclusivity, and equality.

With its colorful streets, charming shops, and lively nightlife, the Castro offers a unique experience for visitors. Here, you can explore the historic Castro Theatre, which has been entertaining audiences since 1922. You can also discover the Castro's many art galleries, vintage boutiques, and antique shops. Take a stroll along the Rainbow Honor Walk, which celebrates the achievements of LGBTQ+ pioneers, or visit the Harvey Milk Plaza, named after the civil rights leader who lived in the neighborhood.

The Castro is also home to some of San Francisco's best restaurants, cafes, and bars.

I now live in San Francisco with my husband Daniel and we’re excited to be Airbnb hosts again. We were super hosts when we lived in Long Beach and loved to share our home with guests from all over the world. 

We look forward to welcoming you to our home.

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish. Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

Hike up Bernal Hill to take in the sweeping views of the City...don't leave without snapping a few pics!

Russian Hill has evolved into a chic residential neighborhood with outstanding views from every corner. Combined with several great cafes, restaurants, antique shops and boutiques, it’s easy to see why any visitor would gladly leave their heart in San Francisco. Cars line up day after day to drive down nearby Lombard Street, the “crookedest” street in the world, and make the slow creep downhill past charming period homes. Polk Street is the main drag in this neighborhood, where you will find trendy bars, cafes and shops populated with locals, but for one of the most charming rides in the city, grab a cable car heading up and down Hyde Street. Aquatic Park and it's small beach are 3 blocks north. The western edge of Fisherman's Wharf and the Buena Vista Cafe, with it's famous Irish Coffees, is two blocks further (east). The view from the rooftop of the apartment includes Aquatic Park, the Golden Gate Bridge and Fisherman's Wharf.

host_about: Originally from Canada, I first came to San Francisco to finish my surgical training at UCSF in the late 1990s, when I moved into the walkup townhouse complex that this studio is a part of. My landlord passed away while I lived there, and I loved the area and the apartment so much that I somehow managed to buy the property from his estate and have continued to live there for many years. I now teach surgical residents for UCSF at their campus in Oakland and have a private practice in Union Square, San Francisco. I have taught surgery and been part of medical missions around the world (Papua New Guinea, Guatemala, Nicaragua, New Zealand, Australia, Canada - including the true "Great White North" around Hudson's Bay). I love to travel to ski, dive, kite board, surf and explore far-off lands and love to visit my family in Toronto and Vancouver - but every time I come home to San Francisco, I take a deep breath and appreciate how fortunate I am to live here!

Historical Telegraph Hill ( VERY SAFE AREA)
Now: The iconic Coit Tower is the focal point of the area for most visitors, but if you're willing to take your time and wander (and hike a couple of steep stretches of steps) you can catch a lot of extra scenery. Many people take the Greenwich Street steps since they are closest to the tower, and return the same way. The Filbert Street steps, just to the south, lead through much more of the lush landscaping characteristic of Telegraph Hill. Our neighborhood is also known for supporting a flock of feral parrots, primarily red-masked parakeets (Aratinga erythrogenys), descended from escaped or released pets. The flock was popularized by a book and subsequent documentary (2003), both titled The Wild Parrots of Telegraph Hill.

Then: The name Telegraph Hill came from a structure built on the top of the hill in the mid-1800s, which would visually signal the city with regard to the type of vessels passing through the Golden Gate.

Diversity. That is the reason I have lived with in 2 blocks of Alamo Square Park for 24 of the 27 years I've lived in San Francisco. This neighborhood is a great mix of people of all colors and ages and the offerings reflect that. The Divisadero corridor (Divisadero from Haight to Golden Gate) is a vibrant street full of all kinds of shops, bars, cafes, restaurants and boutiques. Alamo Square Park itself is a world renowned land mark, beautiful all year round and home of the famous "Painted Ladies" Victorian homes. Yet this area does not have the feel of a "tourist trap" area.
Our neighborhood is now a permit parking zone for street parking. This means that between the hours of 10am and 4pm there is 2 hour limit on street parking for cars without a permit. Parking is free and ample from 4pm to 10am (overnight).

name: Artful Comforts in the Lower Haight
description:
I am rethinking my post COVID listing. Hopefully, the situation will be clearer.
I am fully vaccinated.
As a result of Covid, I thought about lowering my price. I have concluded that I am charging a very fair price for my home. If you like art, paintings and photographs, my home is the place to stay. If you live nearby and you want to stay two nights, I will make an exception. Thanks for considering my home. I have had two vaccines and three boosters
neighborhood_overview: Geographically, I live in the Eureka Valley also known as the sun belt of San Francisco. If the fog burns off, it burns off first in our neighborhood. All public transportation comes to our neighborhood. You can walk to the Mission, Hayes Valley, the Castro and the Civic Center.
host_about:
I live  alone in my our art filled home in the Lower Haight — central to everything. I retired from working downtown in Union Square; it takes very little effort to get there, three stops on MUNI. Our public-transit system is everywhere and very close to the house (be it a MUNI, the N Judah — underground — or the street car on Market Street). Our closest surrounding neighborhoods are Hayes Valley, Duboce Triangle, The Castro (just underwent extensive renovations), the Upper Haight and Valencia Street in the Mission District. On Waller Street we're literally steps away from some of the best food, bars and shopping (not tourist spots). The Lower Haight was voted the number one neighborhood in San Francisco by the tech community. Most important, do not rent a large car or let the car agency upgrade you to a larger car. Parking is too difficult. The rental agency tries to unload larger cars by offering visitors an upgrade. Don't accept it. I allow my guests to park in the street in front of my garage providing there is enough room.

My home (pre earthquake Edwardian) has been with me for more than forty years, so you can ask me anything that you want to know about the Bay Area and I am  bound to point you in the right direction. What else... Ah, just feel free to be in touch. I look forward to having you around! I just concluded my ninth year as a host on Airbnb. I am continually told that my price is too low. I am OK with my fee. I really want my guests to have a great time when staying in my home. To paraphrase the clothing designer Tom Ford, " Surrounding yourself with beautiful objects, enhances the quality of your life". It is my  unofficial motto. 

After hosting many guests from many different places, I learned that it is important to understand that when you book my home you are also experiencing my life. I have friends that stop by. I occasionally have people for dinner. It is essential to understand that I am not a professional innkeeper. I am not running a bed and breakfast. I am an Airbnb host who accept guests to stay in my guest bedrooms. I want my guests to live like residents of San Francisco. My neighborhood is very popular. When you stay with me you are returning to your San Francisco home.

host_about:
Greetings!

My name is Warren C. Lathe III, I go by Trey (a nickname, means "3" :). I am a career biologist (molecular genetics) though currently, I'm writing, teaching and other things (like Airbnb!). 

My partner in crime since 1996, and legal husband since 2008, is Guy and we have two school-age (middle and high schools) children (the picture here was 8 years ago :D). Guy is an English as a Second Language teacher by training and career, but now manages properties.

We have a long and deep connection to San Francisco. Guy is a Berryessa. The Berryessa's settled San Francisco and the bay in the 1770s coming with the De Anza party in 1776. His GGrandfather was Jose de los Santos Berryessa.  Guy's parents were married and lived in this city during the '40s (while his father fought in the Pacific theater). My own parents moved to the Bay Area in the 80's. Guy and I both moved into this home in 1997. San Francisco had been our dream city for its acceptance, tolerance, family heritage and its beauty. It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

Haight street is lined with restaurants, cafes, and great shops. We have three organic grocery markets, including Whole Foods within a five-block walk and a weekly farmers market!

We are right at the Panhandle, just two blocks from Golden Gate Park Park. This huge, beautiful park boasts lakes, fields, an arboretum, a Japanese tea garden, the Conservatory of Flowers, the DeYoung Museum, and the California Academy of Sciences -- the greenest museum in the world, with a living roof, planetarium and tropical rainforest canopy! The park ends at the Pacific Ocean, 4 serene miles from our home. Watch surfers brave the waves of Ocean Beach.

neighborhood_overview:

* Telegraph Hill the most beautiful of San Francisco’s Hills. Intimate and delightful. Possibly also the USA's most famous hill
* One block to the lively cafes, restaurants, bars of North Beach, yet quiet
* Oldest part of San Francisco, part of pre-Gold Rush Yerba Buena
* Rebuilt after 1906 earthquake
* Telegraph Hill got name from pole-and-arm signal station, precursor of internet
* Nearby Coit Tower has perhaps the greatest of urban vistas anywhere

* Beatnik movement centered here, in Caffe Trieste, Vesuv

description: Available for long-term (30 days or more) only - Beautiful and sunny four room flat on a quiet residential street with easy access to public transportation, neighborhood amenities and Golden Gate Park. The flat is fully furnished, has a fabulous kitchen with a Viking Range. Wifi, gas & electricity included. Pet friendly.
neighborhood_overview:
Downey Street is located just off of Haight Street - a SF Landmark neighborhood, and a few blocks away from Cole Valley - a really wonderful family friendly neighborhood with a pharmacy, hardware store, great kid's shop (Tantrum), a dry cleaner, mailing service, and plenty of great places to eat - Zazie (French), Padrecito (great Mexican), La Boulange of SF (breakfast, coffee all day, etc), The Ice Cream Bar (need I say more).

There are lots of local parks and we are just blocks away from Golden Gate Park.
host_about:
Patti manages Downey Street and lives in the flat directly below the rental unit. The building  has a few dogs - a small friendly white dog (the building greeter), a young, enthusiastic hound dog (who likes to protect the building) and a shepherd-mix.  If you are bringing a pet, feel free to ask Patti about local parks, great dog walks and resources such as pet stores, pet sitting, vets and emergency animal hospitals.

Patti owns a design shop in San Francisco's Dogpatch neighborhood . With a background in art and design, she's also a great source of information about the local museums, galleries, etc.

neighborhood_overview:
Nob Hill is one of San Francisco’s historic "Seven Hills" and has long been a symbol of luxury and prestige. The neighborhood rose to prominence in the late 19th century when wealthy railroad tycoons built their grand mansions there, drawn by the area’s commanding views and the convenience of the newly invented cable car, which made the steep incline accessible.

Today, Nob Hill retains its historic charm while blending with modern urban vibrancy. It is known for its elegant architecture, including landmarks like the iconic Fairmont Hotel, Grace Cathedral, and the Mark Hopkins Hotel, which showcase the grandeur of the area’s past. While many of the original mansions were lost in the 1906 earthquake and fire, the neighborhood has evolved into a lively hub with upscale hotels, fine dining, and a large population of young urban professionals.

host_about:
Built by the son of a California Gold Rush miner, the historic Marina Motel was built to celebrate the opening of the Golden Gate Bridge in the late 1930's and is still run by the same family. Ideally situated between Fisherman's Wharf and the Golden Gate Bridge in the popular Marina District, the Marina Motel offers a one-of-a-kind, old world experience. The first impression one has upon stepping into the motel's cobblestone courtyard is "Wow! This is like a little oasis back here with birds chirping, flowers EVERYWHERE, cute little garages and rooms decorated to feel like home. I feel like I'm in Europe."

Walk around the corner to the numerous outdoor cafes, restaurants and boutiques on Chestnut and Union Street, take a walk on the beach to the Golden Gate Bridge or rent a bike and ride across it while taking the ferry back, ride a cable car at Fisherman's Wharf or visit the de Young Museum or California Academy of Science in Golden Gate Park. The best of San Francisco is within easy reach.

name: Peaceful Noe Home with Office and Patio by 24th Street
description:
Welcome to a quiet oasis in Noe!

Noe Valley Luxury Modern is both a family and business traveler friendly space located in a fully rebuilt house that turned a single family cottage from the 1880's into a contemporary multi-level home built for this millennium's lifestyle. High-end finishes and amenities throughout, wonderful indoor-outdoor living spaces, and virtually everything you could possibly need within 2-5 blocks. Think urban boutique hotel - but with a LOT more space!
neighborhood_overview: The home is on a quiet residential street, just off lively 24th Street. It’s an easy walk to everything from Whole Foods and corner burritos, to neighborhood bars and upscale dining. The Noe Valley Saturday Farmers’ Market runs year-round.
host_about:
Andy is a life-long traveler, thrilled to finally be back home in the Bay Area where he grew up and where his extended family still resides.  In 2008 Andy and his wife Tanya were fortunate to find a classic Noe Valley fixer-upper and moved into the cute, tiny Pioneer Victorian where they lived for almost 6 years.  In 2013 they began a complete reconstruction of the 1880's cottage and in 2014 moved their family back into a completely transformed contemporary house equipped for this millenium's lifestyle - the Victorian front remains, but everything behind it now meets the needs and expectations of today (hello, closets and gigabit ethernet...).  Andy has been an at-home Dad since 2000, and has worked in tourism, academia, and as a professional chef.  He loves the vibrant food culture in San Francisco and only wishes he had more time to take advantage of all the amazing arts that San Francisco dishes up on a daily basis as well as the wonderful outdoor spaces, hikes, and bike rides that are nearby.  Andy is very knowledgeable about San Francisco food and fun and is happy to make suggestions to help your stay be enjoyable, fun and tasty, whether you are here for business or family pleasure.

Andy has enjoyed a wide variety of travel styles and accommodations over the years, from $3/night huts on beaches in Eastern Indonesia, simple Ryokan in Japan, and luxury hotels and chateaux in the US, Asia and Europe: the apartment is equipped to closely match the experience of a boutique hotel - luxury finishes throughout and thoughtful amenities - but with a lot more space than most boutique hotels provide!

host_about:
AnneKarin was born in Chicago to Henry P. and Elly Glass.  Theirs was an artistic household.  Henry was educated in the Wiener Werkstadt and was one of the founders of the field of Industrial Design in the U.S.  Elly was a member of the Viennese Dressmakers’ Guild.  Both of them taught at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.  AnneKarin grew up in Northfield IL and graduated from New Trier HS in 1961.  She received her BA in Anthropology from the University of Illinois, Urbana, in 1966 and joined the Peace Corps that same year.  She served as a Volunteer for three years in Ilheus, Bahia, Brazil, where she founded a leather working factory that provided steady work for local shoe makers.  Upon her return she went to Illinois Institute of Technology where she received an MA in Linguistics.
She tolerated the weather in Chicago until 1973 when she moved to San Francisco where Peace Corps friends facilitated her settlement into a new life on the West Coast.  Two months after she arrived she broke her leg in a ski accident and spent 11 months in a cast.  When able to walk again, she pursued a sign painting business which grew into a brokerage for architectural graphics.  From that she moved into print brokering, specializing in 3-D displays.  This enabled her to buy the house she was living in on Potrero Hill in San Francisco.
The recession in 1989 plus the introduction of computer technology into the world of print created a crossroad.  AnneKarin decided to give up the printing business and return to graduate school where she earned a graduate certificate in Educational Therapy.  She specialized in perception/cognition and opened a private practice, helping children and adults with learning disabilities to address the underlying causes of their learning problems.  
During all these years AnneKarin continued to pursue visual art.  Today she works as an artist, focusing on the figure.  When no model is available she enjoys painting still lifes, abstracts, and landscapes.  She has shown her work internationally and in many competitions across the U.S.  She is a member of the Artists’ Guild of San Francisco.
AnneKarin lives with Clebia, whom she met in Ilheus when she was a Peace Corps volunteer. Clebia is a case worker for intellectually challenged adults and a gourmet cook.  Clebia and AnneKarin enjoy travel, walking in the outdoors, fine dining, music, the ballet, who done-its, and old and new friendships.

We are located in the outer Richmond District, halfway up the hill with views of the Pacific Ocean. Adolph Sutro 24th. Mayor of San Francisco, an immigrant, purchased and developed large amounts of property of San Francisco. He developed much of the outer Richmond. He lived here, and developed the Sutro Baths which housed six of the largest indoor swimming pools in the 1880’s. You can visit what is left of his estate at Sutro Park, a short walk. Head up the hill to Anza St. Turn left to Sutro Park. Follow the circular path where you can get a bird's eye view of the pacific as it enters into San Francisco Bay. View Seal Rock and the Cliff House and enjoy the birds which inhabit here. You may want to continue to Land’s End Lookout Visitors Center.

name: Beautiful room in an 1890 Noe Valley Victorian
description:
Beautiful bedroom in a well maintained 1890 Victorian home. Walk to the Mission, 24th St, BART, Muni, Dolores Park.

You have a beautiful, newly remodeled bath shared with one other room. Please forget your past experience of shared baths. Here, all shower shelves, towel bars and cabinets are labeled by room number, creating clear boundaries. Cleaning is regular and you'll likely never find other guests' mess in your way. It's highly organized - just see my reviews.
neighborhood_overview:
Noe Valley is a quiet neighborhood, like a village within a city! It is kind of unique in having about the densest concentration of original Victorian homes dating from the 1850s until the 1900. The reason for the old Victorians (like mine!) is that Noe Valley was miraculously saved from the fire after the 1906 Earthquake because the fire hydrant at 20th and Church Streets was the first found with actual water pressure as the fire raced south from the city center. Earthquake. It served to preserve a firebreak at 20th St. Today you can see 20th century buildings on the North side of 20th and 19th century Victorians on the south side. And don't forget to check out the hydrant, lovingly painted gold.

Noe Valley is surrounded by interesting neighborhoods as well, including the historic and vibrant Latin cultural area called the Mission District as well as the Castro District, famous for it's role in the history of LGBTQ, celebrating many styles of living and loving that were

host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.
- See the Zapatista Mural in Jack Kerouc Alley, painted by a dear friend &  behind iconic City Lights Bookstore .  Ask me about the mural story.
-Catch a baseball game at Oracle park !
SF songs & bands : 
City Lights by Journey
The Grateful Dead of course
Huey Lewis & the News 
Carlos Santana  & more !

host_about: Hi!  We are Tim and Lisa.  These are a few of our favorite things: Our adopted city of San Francisco (we've both lived here over 3 decades), our local neighborhood (the Richmond District), meeting people, nature (birds/beaches/hiking/etc.), live music (especially at SF's fantastic music venues, including the music festivals right here in Golden Gate Park), food, and our family (we have 2 adult daughters and 2 grandkids). Tim comes from a hotel/restaurant family (The Treadway Inns in New England), and now newly retired, he looks forward to returning to his family roots as a friendly and helpful host.  Tim loves to garden and cook. Lisa still happily teaches 2-, 3- and 4-year-olds (coming up on her 31st year at the same school).  Like Tim, she is also from the East Coast (NY).  We put tons of love, care, comfort and quality into building our new apartment, as we expect to live down there ourselves one day.  We currently live upstairs from the apartment and are therefore easy to contact if you need anything (our guests choose how much or little interaction to have with us).  Please let us know if you have any questions!

host_about:
Welcome to HacknSleep! Hacknsleep provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

We partner with startup accelerators, bootcamps, coding academies, and co-working spaces and prefer recruiting our residents through peer-recommendations and our networks. So please let us know how you have heard from us.

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

Separated from the rest of SF and free spirited like the cities of Essos, it’s industrial past has been turned to its advantage with some of the most innovative & eco-friendly industrial condos in the city and like Dorne, is home to some great wine shops & eateries, an eclectic collections of galleries and working art studios. neighborhood_overview:
Our home in the Sunset neighborhood of SF and is perfectly situated to access the entire city using public transportation or walking.

We're close to Inner Sunset and Irving area, Golden Gate Park, and Dim Sum (Irving Street) are walking distance from the house.

Irving street is a bustling corridor of activity, especially weekends. There's so many good restaurants around the corner. Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, Pakistani, Japanese, Middle Eastern, Taiwanese Boba or go to the local and good grocery store around the corner and cook a meal at home.

It's a quiet and safe neighborhood to wander around.

Easy access to both the Ocean Beach and Financial District/Downtown via the L Line Streetcar (45 mins to SoMa via public transit and 20 mins by car).

host_about:
Greetings from Noelle and George!

We both grew up in the Bay Area and are college sweethearts having both majored in biological sciences. We chose to live and raise a family which includes our three children in San Francisco because of the beautiful landscape, amazing culture and diversity, priceless climate and lets not forget exploring this beautiful city through the iconic cable car rides.

As a family we enjoy spending most of our time outdoors which includes hiking in the Marin Headlands, breezy walks along Ocean Beach, as well as biking in Golden Gate Park to name a few. Camping is a major part of our summer routine in Lake Tahoe, Yosemite National Park, and Camp Mendocino. We also enjoy Lake Tahoe during the winter months for skiing and snowboarding. Noelle and I are also avid sports fans and LOVE attending San Francisco Giants, Oakland Athletics, Golden State Warriors, San Francisco Forty Niners, Oakland Raiders and San Jose Shark games with our children and friends. Our weekends are also consumed with youth sports as our children play on baseball, basketball, golf, and swimming teams.

 We are lucky enough to live in an area which embraces the arts and we are just a short stroll away from the many music festivals which San Francisco has to offer and a few of our favorite events to attend are the Blue Grass Festival and Outside Lands both in Golden Gate Park. 

San Francisco offers a variety of multi-cultural cuisine all within a short distance from each other whether it be a walk, drive or door step away. Some of our favorites include, fresh seafood, Pho, Mission-style burritos, Korean BBQ, Cioppino, or exploring our palates with tasting world renowned wine and cheese at the Ferry Building!

neighborhood_overview:
Pacific Heights is one of the nicest historic neighborhoods that is centrally located in San Francisco.
Walking distance to five grocery stores - three blocks to either Whole Foods (one the corner or California street and Franklin street) or Molly Stones (on California street, after you pass Fillmore street). To mor4 blocks to Trader Joe’s and two Safeway’s - I e south and one north from my home, 5 minutes drive. It’s a great place to hike and run. I usually run to the Bay and sometimes to the Golden Gate Bridge and back through Lyon Stairs. Very scenic route. There are lost of beautiful parks close to my home. The closest park is just a 1.5 blocks away - on Laguna and Sacramento street.

host_about:
I am a physician and I moved to USA 22 years ago. I love what San Francisco city and the Bay Area has to offer. I feel very lucky and privileged to live in a beautiful and safe area of San Francisco called Pacific Heights. 

I am an avid mountaineer/climber and I travel usually once a year, for a month - long expedition trip. That is usually when I open the calendar in AirBnB for my apartment, as well as (separately) for my garage. 

I would like to rent my beautiful home to someone reliable for all that time when I am gone. 

The things I can't live without are my family, friends, mountains, my amazing home, nature, meditation and any kind of physical activity daily. 

My favorite travel destinations - to many to mention. I feel amazing in high altitude mountains. 

I climbed all the highest mountains in the world called Seven Summits (including Mt.Everest), as well as skied to the South Pole.  Beside that, all my travels and expeditions left me with amazing memories. 

My favorite books - too many to list here as I  read a lot, but I love the most  "Master and Margarita" by Michail Bulhakov. There are many books in my home, so if you have time feel free to read something new. I switched now to ebooks or audiobooks, as it doesn't take any physical space. 

My favorite food is prepared with local and organic ingredients - check out many restaurants on Fillmore street - you will have so many to choose from, even after Pandemic years. I love sushi and the best sushi in the city is a walking distance from my home - check out Tataki restaurant (on California street/Divisadero street) - amazing and fresh! 
I also would encourage you to check “State Bird Provisions”, but you would need a reservation. It’s a 7 -10 minutes walking distance from my home. Located on Fillmore street. 

I travel a lot for business - Marriott hotels, but for fun - I prefer staying in a tent or in a cool Airbnb place in different cities all over the world. 

My motto in life is to live largely, “on the edge of my comfort zone", hence climbing or polar expeditions, and now posting my home at Airbnb website. 

Throughout the process of renting my home I learn that my HOA’s CC&Rs (Homeowners Rules) do not allow for any short term rentals and I can only rent it for a month or longer. 

My modern apartment is located on the top floor of the beautiful Victorian (freshly painted) building (originally from 1896). I have the best view of Japan Town and Twin Towers as well as complete privacy in my home. 

I love green plants and I have many in my home and at the balcony. I’ll be very grateful if you could please water it once a week ( just a little bit :) to keep it lush and green. 

So far, I had wonderful guests from all over the world for the last ten years. I am super grateful for all people I met through AirBnB. 

Please feel free to ask me any questions before you send a reservation. 

I look forward to meeting you in person and to host you in my home.
 
Thank you.

SAN FRANCISCO – Dogpatch is proof that good things come in small packages. The charming microhood was largely industrial for years, but has become a budding enclave of artisans and craftsmen. The area maintains a sleepy, untouched vibe on the surface — with palpitating creativity at the core.

The historic district is home to some of the city’s oldest structures and Victorian cottages. Pier 70 is an existing shipyard and industrial site that supported both World Wars and manufactured supplies for the Gold Rush and Transcontinental Railway. The Noonan Building at Pier 70 is now studio space.

The area is also becoming the epicenter of micro-manufacturing, with the American Industrial Center (once the old American Can Factory) divided into work spaces that act as incubators for makers of all kinds, from designers and engineers to chefs, artists, and manufacturers.

We have a dog, a house in SF, I'm a crazy serial entrepreneur activist and someone who thinks the world can be a better place if each of us does our part.

host_about:
It’s been said that knowing what someone is grateful for and the challenges they’ve overcome tells you a lot about them. For me there’s nothing in my life that I am more grateful for than my three adult sons who were also my life’s greatest challenge to raise as a single mother in San Francisco.  

In the crucible of parenthood, I have learned so much about working with people and developed qualities that are enormously beneficial in the world of work. When you have children whose lives depend on you, there’s no such thing as “I can’t” or “I’m tired” or “I couldn’t make it happen because…” Year in and year out, in life’s longest marathon, it became a deeply engrained habit to give my best every day and make it happen. 

Being the sole responsible person for three growing boys required discipline, patience, diplomacy, negotiating skills, selflessness, tenacity, compassion, tenderness, endurance, resourcefulness, toughness and, last but not least, a thick skin. These same qualities are the foundation that has allowed me to succeed as an Executive Assistant for top executives at some stimulating and interesting companies, including early stage, privately held, and household-name corporations.  
Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place. 

Namaste!

neighborhood_overview:
Valencia Street is one of the main arteries in San Francisco’s iconic Mission District and one of the emerging hotspots for shopping, dining, nightlife and shopping. It’s worth mentioning shopping twice, as few neighborhoods and commercial strips in the city offer a more funky, interesting and eclectic blend of shops, from local mom-and-pops to trendy national and international niche retailers and all points in-between.

Starting with clothing, you’ll see the obligatory lululemon activewear storefront right next to a local joint selling vintage threads from the 50s and 60s. Trendy spots such as Taylor Stitch and Nooworks offer made-in-America fashions created by local and national designers for hipsters and those wishing to increase their hipness quotient. neighborhood_overview:
The vibrant 24th Street commercial area with its restaurants, cafes, and Saturday farmers market, and Whole Foods is an easy 10 minute walk. Church street, just a block away from the home, offers additional dining and cafe options along with the J-Church tram, which takes you to downtown and beyond.

Valencia Street, arguably the hippest area in all of San Francisco, is within walking distance of 15 minutes. While there, be sure to stroll around Dolores Park to take in the city view, and make stops at Tartine Bakery and Bi-Rite Creamery, two of the many gems in the area.

Within 10 minutes is Mitchell's Ice Cream, a neighborhood staple since 1955. A block away from that is Safeway.

Another nearby neighborhood within a 15-20 minute walk is Glen Park, where you can hike the Glen Canyon trails up to Twin Peaks, the highest peak in the city with panoramic views of the entire city, or take BART, the area's train system to access all of the Bay Area.

name: Modern Private Suite in the Mission
description: Modern separate suite (~450 sq ft) in the colorful Mission district. Separate entrance, en-suite bathroom, mini fridge and microwave. Steps from Mexican food, sushi, bookstores, murals & several bus lines.  10 min walk to BART.
neighborhood_overview:
The Mission is a fun and vibrant neighborhood - there is so much to do and see here! We see eating tours and mural viewing tours in and around our neighborhood all the time. A few times a year, there are parades that go down 24th Street, such as for Dia de los Muertos, Carnaval, and Cinco de Mayo.

We are just a few minutes walk from some of the city's most popular restaurants and food establishments including: Flour + Water, Dynamo Donuts, Humphrey Slocombe (unique ice cream), and Farmhouse Kitchen Thai. Visit Dandelion Chocolate for a tour! Heath Ceramics and Tartine Manufactory are also nearby.

The Mission has one of the warmest microclimates in the city, so we get a lot of sun and less fog than other areas.

neighborhood_overview:
Music City Hotel is located in the vibrant Polk Gulch/Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

Tourist attractions and neighborhoods

neighborhood_overview:
Noe Valley feels like a small town despite its centrality in San Francisco, making it a coveted neighborhood. As the name suggests it's bordered by hills, giving it an intimate feel. 24th Street is its main drag, full of artisanal goods stores, yoga places, and a Whole Foods.

It has a very cohesive community feeling, as evidenced by the brand new town square that sits off of 24th Street; this is the result of an organized effort by residents to turn a parking lot into a space to gather and relax in the sun. The town square now houses the wonderful Saturday Farmer’s Market, which features live music, food carts and local produce.

Noe Valley is sunny and clean-cut, with lots of pedestrians, many with strollers and dogs. Bordered on the north by The Castro and Dolores Heights, on the east by The Mission, on the south by Glen Park, and on the west by Diamond Heights and Twin Peaks.

neighborhood_overview: It's The Mission District. a bit gritty but the place to be stationed. Named for Mission Dolores founded in 1776, San Francisco’s oldest neighborhood has some of its hottest new restaurants and galleries. Bernal Heights, Potrero Hill These neighborhoods all share a sunny outlook. Boasting some of the best weather in the city, the Mission District, Bernal Heights and Potrero Hill take advantage of an abundance of fog-free days. My place faces west so it's on the street side and is usually quite noisy from people, traffic and sirens. Thankfully the residence was constructed in 2008 and  built  quite soundproof. The bedrooms are well sized and comfortably appointed. The sun always seems to shine in the Mission District.

Finally, I love being an AirBnB host which allows me to share my good fortune, meet wonderful people and make new friends. 

I hope that you choose to stay. 

Mark

host_about:
My wife and I have traveled the world, but have called San Francisco home for 25 years. We invite you to stay with us in our 1896 Edwardian home in the middle of the Mission District, San Francisco's oldest and arguably most vibrant neighborhood filled with a diverse range of some of the City's best restaurants, bars, parks, shops, and more. Not to mention our neighborhood is the warmest, flattest, and fog free part of San Francisco. 

We're 15 minutes from SFO by taxi, a block and a half from the 24th Bart Station and close to many bus and MUNI (subway) lines. Having visited Southeast Asia, Oceania, Australia, Europe, Central America, and of course all over North America, one theme holds true for all our adventures: discover the true culture and flavor wherever we are. 

As your host, we'll do everything we can to make sure you get off the beaten path. We're happy to share our favorite restaurants, local hangouts, and ensure you see the true San Francisco, not just the typical touristy sites. We're into everything from scuba diving, biking, kayaking, hiking, wine, art, music, food, festivals, museums, all things teens, parks, and more. Whatever you're into, we'll point you in the right direction so you have an authentic and memorable time in San Francisco. My motto is from the great Mahatma Ghandi: "Be the change you wish to see in the world." Our style of hosting reflects the needs of our guests. When possible, we like to meet our guests. However we understand that many of them are busy on a tight schedule or not interested to meet us so we respect that. We want to make sure every guest is comfortable and part of that is respecting boundaries and their personal space. 

We look forward to hosting you soon! If you have any questions, please feel free to ask. We're just a click away.

name: Peaceful Noe Valley private space near everything
description:
Peaceful and charming 2 room, 1 bath space with private entrance.

Sanitized in between stays!

This is your own private area in my home in a great San Francisco neighborhood. Tranquil bedroom. "Living room" w/ tv with cable, sofa sleeper, and fridge.

In one of SF's most sought-after neighborhoods.

1/2 block from public transport, walk to cafes, restaurants, bars, the Castro and the mission :)
Easy parking, by SF standards!
neighborhood_overview:
Noe Valley has become one of the most sought-after neighborhoods in all of San Francisco (and maybe the country), and for very good reason. It is central, located close to freeways and public transportation. It has quaint tree-lined streets, and is full of fantastic cafés restaurants and shops.

My home is a quick 8-10 minute walk from vibrant 24th St. and a 15 to 20 minute walk from Dolores Park and the trendy and famous Mission district, home to some of the best Mexican food in the country.

There are buses that leave a half block away from the house every 10 to 20 minutes that will take you anywhere you want to go in San Francisco, and light rail just 3 blocks away. The Marina, Golden Gate Park, china town, or fisherman's wharf are all just a short drive or bus ride away.
host_about:
Born and raised in CA. I'm a former management consultant turned lawyer, actor (used to be pretty busy with this, now I'm not in LA enough to be serious about it), and surfer/paddleboarder. Only a decent surfer, trying to get better. Not the most typical of career combinations, lol.

I just moved to San Francisco from southern california (santa monica, to be exact) but grew up in the bay area. I LOVE San Francisco...though I wish the beaches were a bit warmer! 

I used to Airbnb my place in Santa Monica and met some great people doing that.  Now that I'm in SF, I hope to make my place and extra space available when I don't need it. 

I have simple tastes and believe happiness comes from good friends/family and great experiences, rather than having too many expensive things. 

I strive to be a good host by communicating with my guests and providing extra little touches to make your stay fun and comfortable. So if you have questions, just ask :)

host_about:
I have been a happy resident of San Francisco since 1994, living right here on McAllister St where I arrived after a former life-time married to a fine man, raising a family of three sons.
I came for a visit and decided to stay......San Francisco does that to you.  I spent my early years here touring the city on inline skates, yes, hills and flat....great adventures, great friends, did the Friday Night Skate for years.   My work and rental property take my time and the fact that I now have 5 dear grandchildren living around the country means I travel rather often.  Now I walk everywhere with Muni as a backup.  SF is a great place to walk, you are never at a loss to find interesting places, beautiful buildings and lovely parks, beaches, trails, whatever your heart desires.  Good way to keep healthy, too, with yoga and gardening added for balance.  I have been renting rooms in my place since 1997 when I was able to purchase it.  I have had hundreds of people stay since then, many from other countries.  I have furnished rooms and cater to students, interns, people new to the city, beginning jobs.....a good place to get a start and figure out where you want to stay more permanently.  I try to make it a home away from home for them.  For me it is like having a large, ever changing family.
Because of the changing politics throughout the world, much of which is troubling,  as angry people take over governments and spread upset and anger about, I think it is valuable to have platforms such as Airbnb bringing people together from everywhere.  The chance to meet, talk, share a meal, converse with a group of people from different countries has to be good for our world.  I have a large map of the world in the living room and each guest puts a pin in the country from which they come.  It is thrilling to see the map fill and know that we have had good times with friends from all of those places!

Food
The Mission district is famous and influential for its restaurants. A number of Mission restaurants have gained national attention, most notably the five restaurants who have received Michelin stars for 2017: Commonwealth, Lazy Bear, Aster, Californios, and Al’s Place. A large number of other restaurants are also popular, including: Mission Chinese Food, Bar Tartine, La Taqueria, Foreign Cinema on Mission Street, Delfina, Lolinda, Flower & Water, Central Kitchen, Trick Dog, and Locanda. Dozens of taquerías are located throughout the neighborhood, showcasing a localized styling of Mexican food. There is also a high concentration of Salvadoran, Guatemalan, and Nicaraguan restaurants as well as street food

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

Flywheel Coffee Roasters is a flashy new coffee shop and roastery with a decent amount of seating and coworking. 2 blocks west at 672 Stanyan street.
Reverie Cafe several blocks south at 848 Cole St. and has a lovely garden patio.
Cafe International a bit further down haight is a local treasure

Bars
Zam Zam is the original haight street bar with the famous round bar. Open since 1941. Half a block east at 1633 Haight Street.
Alembic has a mean Old Fashioned and other classic cocktails, as well as modern twists on all of the above. 1 block west at 1725 Haight Street.

Irving and 9th Ave are the central streets full of families and friends catching a bite to eat - often after strolling in Golden Gate Park or doing some shopping.

The neighborhood is bordered by lush Golden Gate Park, with two museums, a concourse with live music on most Sundays and more green space than you’d expect.

neighborhood_overview: Great location! Lone Mountain/NOPA is a charming and safe residential neighborhood centrally located  in San Francisco, close to many hospitals and both Golden Gate Park and Presidio parks, with great transit options nearby.  You can be downtown or to CPMC in less than 20 minutes on the bus, or walking among fountains, parks and museums in 5. host_about:
Hi.  I've lived in SF for more than 25 years, and have fallen completely in love with it's quirky, charming, eccentric, exciting ways.  Now I love the opportunity to share my love of SF with others!  My garden apartment is a fully self-contained 1 bedroom unit,  downstairs from my own home in a 1885 Victorian, but completely private except for the shared back garden and patio.  I have outfitted it with everything I could think of that helps make a visit comfortable, from good books to good coffee and olive oil to comfy furniture and luxurious towels and sheets. 

I love living in this charming neighborhood near Golden Gate park, less than 3 miles from  downtown San Francisco and less than 1 mile from the trendy NOPA restaurants and only 3 blocks from the many great ethnic restaurants on Clement street. I  love walking, hiking and biking in the nearby parks and visiting the neighborhood museums and restaurants.  

I'm a trained mediator and also teach English as a Second Language (certified by Cambridge University) and am pleased to give you tips for visitors from other countries (or private English lessons, at a discount!)   

I love to travel myself (next goal is Egypt and Jordan), and try to treat all guests as I like to be treated when away from home.   

My goal is to give each guest all the privacy that they prefer.  I'm available if you'd like, or will respect your private sanctuary if that's your preference. 

 I hope you'll love living like a local in San Francisco as much as I do!

neighborhood_overview:
The Mission District's multifarious corridors comprise an inviting melting pot of cultures, cuisines, and cool kids. Produce bins line the sidewalks in front of colorful Latino markets, and the aroma of fresh roasted coffee beans emanates from first-class cafes along this diverse neighborhood’s main streets. Whether you’re looking for upscale restaurants, lowbrow dive bars, the best taquerias, or simply delicious street food, the Mission delivers.

Around the corner from the flat you have Blue Bottle coffee which is one of our best locally produced coffees. It shares a space with Heath Ceramics, a nationally recognized and much respected pottery business that's fun to browse. In the neighborhood itself, not only do you have many choices of delicious Mexican food, but you will find Blowfish Sushi, one of the most sought after sushi restaurants in the city. It's a fun little area to explore on foot, with some unexpected hidden gems you can stumble upon.

description: Enjoy a peaceful retreat and/or remote office space in an updated private studio apartment steps away from Precita Park & Bernal Hill and an easy commute down the peninsula.  Easy & safe street parking (no meters/limitations).  Nearby restaurants, cafes & groceries.  Short walk to 24th St in the Mission. neighborhood_overview:
Precita Park is a 1-2 minute walk down the hill and is a quiet and typically sunny grass field lined with trees and dotted at its edges with cafes, restaurants, and a natural foods market (Harvest Hills). It's a great venue for a sunny day either with friends or to relax on your own.

Bernal Hill is very easily accessible via the Norwich St exit from the studio. The top-most portion of the hill - where you can get stunning views of most of the city and much of the greater bay area - can be reached in a ten-minute jog or ~20 minute walk from the studio.

Both Treat Avenue and Norwich Street (which dead-ends at the property) are dead-end streets and so there is very little traffic to speak of.

Mission St is a 10-minute walk from the studio and has a large selection of bars & restaurants nearby (see Guidebook for details).

The 24th Street corridor of the Mission district is a 12-minute walk away. See Guidebook for recommendations.
